neutral_facts.value: The accused, who was not in good terms with his wife and her family, was the uncle of the deceased, who was the son of his elder sister. The deceased had developed a close relationship with the accused's daughter, which angered the accused. The deceased visited the accused's house, where he was questioned about his intentions. The accused became enraged and stabbed the deceased multiple times with a knife. The deceased's body was found in the accused's compound. The accused and his daughters went to the police station and handed over the knife. The prosecution relied on the presence of the deceased's body, the knife found at the scene, and the testimony of the accused's daughters, despite their hostile demeanor. The trial court considered the circumstantial evidence, including the forensic science laboratory report confirming human blood on the knife, and convicted the accused of murder.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused, enraged by the deceased's attempt to develop a close relationship with his daughter, stabbed the deceased multiple times with a knife and handed it over to the police. The evidence, including the FSL report and the presence of the dead body in the accused's compound, supported the prosecution's case.

quotes.text: The accused ... stabbed the deceased ... handed over the knife to the police ... FSL report ... dead body in the compound of the accused.
The FSL report also confirmed that human blood was found on the weapon (M.0.-10) though the origin of the blood group was stated to be not traceable.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the eye-witnesses, PW-1 and PW-2, turned hostile, and their testimony could not be relied upon. Additionally, the witnesses related to the deceased (PW-3, 4, 6, and 7) were also biased, and there was no incriminating evidence connecting the accused to the death of the deceased.

quotes.text: The so-called eye-witnesses, namely, PW-1 and PW-2, having turned hostile, Ext P-1 could not be acted upon;
Merely because PWs-3, 4, 6 and 7 are related to the deceased, there is no reason why they should implicate the appellant who is also closely related to them.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that circumstantial evidence, when properly analyzed and corroborated, can lead to a conviction. The court emphasized that the presence of the accused at the police station and the corroborative evidence of the deceased's injuries supported the prosecution's case.

quotes.text: The trial court has rightly held that though the two eye-witnesses fumed hostile, their presence at the police station was admitted and correctness of the report given by one of them at the police station could not be questioned.
The overall consideration of the evidence available on record only substantiates the guilt of the accused in the killing of the deceased.

sentencing_rationale.value: The accused was sentenced to life imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 1,000/- with a default sentence of three months of simple imprisonment due to the overwhelming evidence of his guilt, including the presence of the dead body in his compound, the FSL report, and the testimony of the prosecution witnesses.

quotes.text: The trial Court ... imposed the sentence of imprisonment for life apart from a fine of Rs. 1000/- with a default sentence of three months of simple imprisonment.
